Shipping an Unreal Engine game to Android

Aether Architect is a third-person Unreal Engine 5.8 adventure for Android - floating islands, crystal pickups, motion-matching locomotion. Desktop Unreal habits do not survive the trip to a phone. This is what actually broke, and what fixed it.

Touch is a different control scheme, not a smaller one

A thumb is not a mouse. The first build assumed a virtual stick plus a look area, and it was unplayable: the camera fought the movement stick, and taps intended for the camera landed on UI. What worked was treating the screen as three zones - movement, look, and action - with dead zones that never overlap.

  • Movement bottom-left, relative to the character, not the camera.
  • Look everywhere else, with sensitivity that scales with frame rate.
  • Action a dedicated button that cannot be triggered by the look area.

Thermal throttling is the real performance target

A phone holds its peak frame rate for a minute, then the SoC heats up and the clock drops. Benchmarking on a cold device is meaningless. The target was not "60 fps" - it was "still playable after fifteen minutes", which meant designing for the throttled state from the start.

Concretely: dynamic resolution scaling that responds to sustained frame time rather than instantaneous spikes, and a hard cap on shadow-casting lights. The scene looks the same at the throttled resolution; it just stops trying to render what nobody can see.

Motion matching costs differently than you expect

PoseSearch and the Animation Locomotion Library are excellent on desktop. On mobile the cost is not the search - it is the memory. The pose database is large, and a phone will evict it under pressure, at which point every locomotion query misses and the character starts sliding.

The fix was shrinking the database rather than the search: fewer poses, chosen for the actual movement set of the game, with a fallback blend for the gaps. A small database that always hits beats a large one that pages out.

Packaging: the part nobody warns you about

  • Android Gradle plugin mismatch. UE 5.8 expects a specific Gradle and JDK; mixing them fails late, at packaging, with an error that points nowhere useful.
  • ABI splits. Ship arm64 only unless you have a reason; the APK doubles otherwise.
  • Asset cook size. Cooked content is far larger than the source. Texture compression settings matter more than resolution.
  • First-run shader compilation. A cold install stutters on the first level load; precompiling the PSO cache removes it.

What I would do differently

Test on a thermally throttled device from day one, not at the end. Every performance decision I made was against a cold phone, and the last two weeks went on re-tuning what should have been tuned from the start.
